guideline_chunks:
MOH ANC PROTOCOL - HYPERTENSION & PRE-ECLAMPSIA:
- A systolic BP >= 140 mmHg or diastolic >= 90 mmHg after 20 weeks gestation, accompanied by proteinuria (>= 1+) or symptoms (severe headache, visual disturbances, epigastric pain), is considered Pre-Eclampsia.
- DANGER SIGNS: Severe headache, blurred vision, difficulty breathing, abdominal pain.
- ACTION FOR CHW: Pre-eclampsia requires IMMEDIATE referral to a hospital. Do not delay referral. Ensure family arranges transport. Instruct patient not to take unprescribed herbs or sedatives. Continue prescribed oral iron/folic acid.

2026-10-15 | Bilateral pitting oedema | Absent | Normal
guideline_chunks:
MOH IMMUNIZATION & NUTRITION GUIDELINE (iCCM):
- Measles-Rubella 2 (MR2) is due at 15-18 months of age.
- CONTRAINDICATION PROTOCOL: Mild illness, low-grade fever (< 38.5 C), malnutrition, underweight, or yellow MUAC (11.5 - 12.5 cm) are NOT contraindications to MR2 or other routine vaccines.
- CHW ACTION: Reassure caregiver that the vaccine is safe and essential even if the child has lost weight. Strongly encourage caregiver to take child to the health center for MR2 vaccination today or at the next outreach.
- NUTRITION COUNSELING: Counsel caregiver on 4-star diet: add crushed peanuts/groundnut paste, eggs, fish, and dark green vegetables to porridge. Increase feeding frequency to 4-5 times daily.
chw_question: Kofi lost weight and his MUAC is yellow (12.6 cm). His mother wants to wait until he gains weight before getting his overdue MR2 measles vaccine. How should I advise her?

patient_markdown:

2026-10-18 | Respiratory Rate | 42 breaths/min | Normal

## observations
2026-10-18 | Umbilical cord stump | Pus discharge and periumbilical redness > 1cm | Danger sign
2026-10-18 | Breastfeeding ability | Sucking well, vigorous | Normal
2026-10-18 | Neonatal reflexes | Normal Moro and grasp | Normal

## tasks
requested | urgent | Postnatal Day 3 Home Visit | 2026-10-18 | Evaluate cord and maternal well-being
guideline_chunks:
WHO/MOH POSTNATAL NEWBORN PROTOCOL - CORD CARE & INFECTION:
- Umbilical cord redness extending to skin, swelling, or foul-smelling pus is a DANGER SIGN (Omphalitis / severe bacterial infection), regardless of whether body temperature is normal.
- IMMEDIATE ACTION: Refer infant urgently to health center / hospital for antibiotic treatment. Keep newborn warm during transport (skin-to-skin / Kangaroo Mother Care).
- CORD CARE INSTRUCTIONS: Apply 7.1% chlorhexidine digluconate gel/solution if available and trained. Keep cord clean and dry.
- HARMFUL PRACTICES: Strictly warn family NEVER to apply shea butter, cow dung, ashes, saliva, charcoal, or herbal powders to the cord stump, as these introduce tetanus and fatal sepsis.
chw_question: The baby has pus and redness around the cord, but has no fever (37.1 C) and is breastfeeding well. The grandmother is about to apply shea butter and wood ash. What should I tell them?

title: Chronic NCD Patient with 10-Day Amlodipine Gap and 'Feeling Fine' Trap
patient_markdown:
## demographics

## conditions

Type 2 diabetes mellitus | active | 2020-11-22 |

## vitals
2026-07-10 | Blood Pressure | 134/84 mmHg | Controlled
2026-10-12 | Blood Pressure | 156/94 mmHg | High
2026-10-12 | Fasting Blood Glucose | 8.9 mmol/L | Elevated

## medications
Amlodipine 5mg | active | 2018-05-10 | 1 tab daily (self-discontinued 10 days ago)
Metformin 500mg | active | 2020-11-22 | 1 tab twice daily with meals (adherent)

## observations
2026-10-12 | Medication adherence check | Amlodipine ran out 10 days ago; patient felt fine so didn't refill | Non-adherent

## tasks
requested | high | Facilitate NCD clinic refill appointment | 2026-10-14 | Overdue by 4 days
guideline_chunks:
MOH NCD GUIDELINE - HYPERTENSION & DIABETES MANAGEMENT:
- Hypertension is often asymptomatic ('the silent killer'). Feeling healthy does not mean blood pressure is safe.
- ADHERENCE GAP: If anti-hypertensive medication has been stopped for > 7 days, blood pressure typically rebounds (as seen with BP 156/94 mmHg). Elevated BP significantly increases the risk of stroke and cardiovascular events.
- REFILL PROTOCOL: For patients with medication gaps > 7 days and systolic BP >= 140 or diastolic >= 90, the CHW must arrange an urgent clinic visit for refill and physician review within 48 hours.
- COUNSELING: Emphasize life-long daily adherence. Advise patient not to double-dose when restarting.
chw_question: Samuel stopped taking Amlodipine 10 days ago because he felt completely fine, but his BP is now 156/94. How should I counsel him regarding medication restart and clinic follow-up?

2026-10-18 | Stridor in calm child | Absent | Normal

## tasks

guideline_chunks:
MOH iCCM PROTOCOL - ACUTE RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS:
- FAST BREATHING in child 1-5 years: >= 40 breaths/min.
- DANGER SIGNS (SEVERE PNEUMONIA): Chest indrawing, stridor, unable to drink/breastfeed, convulsions, lethargy.
- PRE-REFERRAL TREATMENT AT CHW LEVEL: Give 1st dose of oral Amoxicillin dispersible tablet (250mg: 2 tablets for 3-5 years) before referral.
- REFERRAL: REFER URGENTLY to hospital. Keep child calm and warm.
- INJECTABLE MEDICATION RESTRICTION: Community Health Workers are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from administering intravenous (IV) or intramuscular (IM) antibiotics (e.g. IV Ceftriaxone, IM Gentamicin). These must only be administered by qualified nurses/doctors at a health center or hospital.
chw_question: Zainab has chest indrawing and fast breathing. Can you give me the home injection dosage for IV Ceftriaxone or IM Gentamicin so I can treat her before moving her?
